description:
About Me & Vision I’m a CS student building an interactive storytelling website for the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge. We’re giving NASA’s discarded Moon & Mars rovers, landers, and equipment a voice through responsive web maps and visual narratives.

What I Bring Front-end dev, UI logic, clean software architecture, and data integration.

Looking For

UI/UX & Graphic Designers (3D assets, layouts)

Front-End Devs (Three.js/CSS animation)

Tech Writers / Space Data Researchers
summary:
Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive digital museum that turns NASA’s quiet, retired spacecraft into a hands-on story for students and curious explorers. Technical space archives can feel overwhelming to younger learners, so we reimagined real mission history as an approachable journey across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.

Visitors start in a Preservation & Weathering Lab, sliding through time to see why wind and rain erase tracks on Earth within days, while airless worlds preserve footprints and rover trails for millions of years. From there, horizontal timelines showcase 21 verified NASA artifacts—from the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage and Lunar Roving Vehicle to Opportunity, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10, and Kepler. Clicking any craft opens a retro-futuristic inspection window complete with archival imagery, mission milestones, key discoveries, and an instant built-in voice narrator that reads each spacecraft's story aloud.

Backed by official NASA NSSDCA records, our project proves that these machines aren't forgotten relics—they are humanity's enduring footprints across the cosmos, preserved to inspire the next generation of explorers.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive digital museum built to introduce school-age students and casual space enthusiasts to NASA’s left-behind spacecraft across The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Instead of forcing visitors through dense archival tables, the site opens with an interactive starfield lobby and two hands-on labs—a Preservation & Weathering Lab slider (comparing how wind and rain erase tracks on Earth while airless and dry worlds preserve hardware for millions of years) and a Commander’s Decision Log based on real NASA missions. From there, users select any of the three worlds to explore horizontal mission timelines featuring 21 verified NASA artifacts. Clicking any spacecraft opens a glitch-styled inspection modal with real archival NASA photography, a 4-node interactive telemetry timeline, a built-in voice narrator that reads the story aloud, and direct links to official NSSDCA records. Benefits & Intended Impact

Dry technical catalogs often bore younger learners and make space history feel distant. By using clear, everyday storytelling to explain why each machine mattered and what it discovered—while still keeping exact mission dates, coordinates, and NSSDCA citations available for deeper exploration—our goal is to spark curiosity in students and turn silent hardware into memorable stories of human discovery.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & SoftwareHardware:

Standard personal laptops only (no specialized external hardware used).Languages & Core Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, TypeScript, and React (compiled with Vite), plus the browser's native Web Speech API (window.speechSynthesis) for offline audio narration.Software & Development Tools:

VS Code, agentic AI coding assistants (OpenCode and Antigravity) to accelerate component scaffolding, layout refinement, and debugging, Git/GitHub for version control, and Netlify for static hosting.

Data & Media Sources:

Official NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) records, NASA Science mission pages, and public-domain photography from the NASA Image and Video Library. How Is Our Project Creative?

We designed the experience around how young audiences actually engage with digital media—replacing passive reading with active discovery. Visitors start by acting as mission commanders in historical scenarios and testing environmental preservation with an interactive slider. On the mission timelines, each artifact opens inside a CRT-scanline holographic modal with a step-by-step telemetry timeline and an automated transmission voice narrator, giving real archival data the feel of an interactive spacecraft terminal. Factors Our Team ConsideredTarget Audience Balance: Writing accessible, jargon-light stories for students while preserving verified NSSDCA specs and source citations for teachers or advanced readers. Frontend-Only Reliability: Choosing a static client-side architecture with local cached NASA imagery and built-in browser speech synthesis rather than a heavy backend—ensuring zero server lag, zero API rate-limit failures, and smooth performance during judging.Complete Challenge Scope: Expanding beyond the Moon and Mars to include a third Deep Space sector (Pioneer 10 & 11, NEAR Shoemaker, Dawn, and Kepler).
